statement: A generic consequence-class taxonomy (what kind of consequence an action carries) must never be bent to control which enforcement mechanism processes that action. When a system needs two services to share the same honest consequence classification while being governed by two different, mutually exclusive enforcement mechanisms, it MUST introduce a second, independent discriminator for 'which mechanism governs this' rather than misclassifying the shared axis to produce the desired mechanism side effect. A frozen gate's exception scope (e.g. 'only capability X may request mode Y') must be satisfied by choosing which request that gate receives, never by lying about the requester's own classification.
classification: A single-axis-doing-two-jobs defect: `serviceClass` was overloaded to answer both 'what kind of consequence' and 'which gate mode to request', so satisfying the second question for a second CONSEQUENTIAL service required falsifying the answer to the first. The generic shape is any classification field that a gate/router also reads to select behavior — the moment two truthfully-same-classified things need different gate behavior, a second explicit discriminator is required rather than bending the shared classification.

canaries.assertion: MONEYPENNY_RUNTIME and MONEYPENNY_RUNTIME_CONSTITUTIONAL both declare serviceClass: 'CONSEQUENTIAL'; they declare different governancePath values (CONSTITUTIONAL_COMMERCE vs CONSTITUTIONAL_SERVICE_PIPELINE); GOVERNANCE_PATH_EXECUTION_MODE_OVERRIDE, not SERVICE_CLASS_EXECUTION_MODE, determines which one requests Gate 2's authoritative mode; Gate 2's own source is unchanged.

occurrences.defect: MONEYPENNY_RUNTIME_CONSTITUTIONAL declared serviceClass: 'PROPOSAL' — a false consequence classification — purely to make it request Gate 2's unconditionally-passed 'shadow' mode and avoid the authoritative-mode refusal, when the service genuinely binds real financial consequence via the constitutional service pipeline.

notes: Sibling to CI-2026-08-23-PROJECTION-GATED-ON-EXECUTION-REACHABILITY-001 (a caller must gate an expensive computation on the callee's own declared need for it) — that invariant governs a CALLER's behavior; this one governs how a CATALOG/DEFINITION represents itself so callers never have a reason to misread it.

The reusable diagnostic question for a future reviewer: 'is this classification field being read by more than one downstream decision, and would satisfying one reading require lying to the other?' If yes, split the axis.
